LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                              MINUTES FROM OCTOBER 22, 2026
                                       OPEN SESSION

MINUTES OF OCTOBER 22, 2026 OPEN SESSION OF THE LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE
COMMISSION HELD IN NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA. PRESENT WERE CHAIRMAN ERIC
SKRMETTA, VICE CHAIRMAN JEAN-PAUL COUSSAN, COMMISSIONER FOSTER CAMPBELL,
COMMISSIONER MIKE FRANCIS, COMMISSIONER DAVANTE LEWIS, AND EXECUTIVE
SECRETARY BRANDON FREY.

Open Session of October 22, 2026, convening at 10:15 a.m., and adjourning at 1:33 p.m., at the Louisiana
Supreme Court Building, 400 Royal Street, New Orleans, Louisiana, with the above-named members of
the Commission and Executive Secretary Brandon Frey present.

 Ex. 1          Chairman Skrmetta thanked Justice William H. Burris for allowing the Commission to use the
                Louisiana Supreme Court building for its meeting.
                Commissioner Lewis thanked everyone who participated in Senator Barrow’s Utility
                Assistance Coordination Taskforce meeting pertaining to Senate Resolution 148. He also
                congratulated Entergy Louisiana, LLC and 1803 Electric Cooperative, Inc. for receiving the
                Department of Energy’s Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key
                Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades (SPARK) grants.
                Executive Counsel Kathryn Bowman announced that the first public meeting for the Energy
                Efficiency Working Group will be held Thursday, November 5, 2026, at the Commission’s
                Office, 12th Floor Conference Room in the Galvez Building at 10:30 A.M.
 Ex. 2          T-37136 - Cantium, LLC vs. Rosefield Fourchon Operating, LLC. In re: Complaint against
                Rosefield for transportation and terminaling of crude oil as a Common Carrier without a tariff
                on file with the Commission at rates that are excessive and request that Rosefield pay
                reparations, refunds and damages for charges above just and reasonable rates.
                In re: Discussion and possible vote on Final Recommendation on Remand of the
                Administrative Law Judge.

                After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, and
                unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Final Recommendation on Remand
                of the Administrative Law Judge issued in the form of a Draft Order filed into the record on
                October 7, 2026, which concludes that the Commission’s finding of Rosefield as a common
                carrier is not altered based upon the applicability of the Louisiana Revised Statutes amended
                in Act 458 of the 2025 Legislative Session.

                Present for Questions/Comments:
                Jamie Watts – Counsel for Rosefield Fourchon Operating, LLC
                Seth Lawrence - Counsel for Rosefield Fourchon Operating, LLC
                Matt Simone – Counsel for Cantium, LLC




                                                     -1-               Minutes of October 22, 2026 B&E
 Ex. 3   T-38039 - Louisiana Public Service Commission vs. Next Nest, LLC. In re: Alleged violation
        of La. R.S. 45:161 through 180.1, by engaging in activities related to moving household goods
        prior to complying with the requirements of La. R.S. 45:164 (E) and General Order dated
        March 16, 2021 and for failure to comply with the requirements of General Order dated April
        3, 2008 as amended.
        In re: Discussion and possible vote pursuant to Rule 57 on Affidavit and Stipulation
        executed by the carrier.
        On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously
        adopted, the Commission voted to exercise its original and primary jurisdiction pursuant to
        Rule 57.
        On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously
        adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Affidavit and Stipulation executed on September
        25, 2026 for fines and fees totaling $525.
Ex. 4   R-36241 - Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte In re: Rulemaking to Revise the
        Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure.
        In re: Discussion and possible vote on Staff's Recommendation of Final Proposed Rules
        for Part 2-Parties.

        After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, and
        unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to adopt the Final Proposed Rules filed into the
        record on October 7, 2026.

        Present for Questions/Comments:
        Ahmed Jabar – Take Back the Power and Louisiana Party for Socialism and Liberation
        Daniel Erspamer – CEO of Pelican Institute for Public Policy
Ex. 5   R-37871 - Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: Louisiana Advanced Nuclear
        Exploration Program.
        In re: Discussion and possible vote on Final Rule.

        After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, with
        Commissioner Campbell and Commissioner Francis concurring, and Commissioner Lewis
        opposing, the Commission voted to adopt the Final Rules filed into the record on August 6,
        2026 with amendments. The motion passed 4:1.

        Chairman Skrmetta’s motion was to adopt the Final Rules with amendments as follows: : I
        move to accept the final proposed rules filed into the record on August 6th with four
        modifications, intended to avoid per meter charges or rate increases for customers as a result
        of the rule. The first modification is to replace the entirety of Section 201 and replace it with
        the following. “Each participating utility is authorized to spend up to $2 million over three
        years on approved program activities. Any such expenditures are subject to review for
        prudence and accordance with applicable law. Prudently incurred expenditures on approved
        program activities are deemed eligible for recovery through base rates so long as those
        expenditures do not result in a rate increase for customers.”
        The second modification is to delete Section 101(A)(1) and Section 501(B) as they are now
        unnecessary with the changes made to Section 201.
        The third modification is to change the term of the program in Section 501 from five years to
        three years.
        The fourth modification is to change Section 101(A) from “enable” to “require” as the intent
                                              -2-                Minutes of October 22, 2026 B&E
         of the program and the rule was to require the IOUs to participate and also allow interested
        cooperatives to participate.
        Present for Questions/Comments:
        Kendall Barry – Take Back the Power and Louisiana Party for Socialism and Liberation
Ex. 6   R-37943 - Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: Possible modifications to
        General Order dated October 12, 2007 related to franchise fees.
        In re: Discussion and possible vote on Staff's Final Proposed Rule and Recommendation.

        After discussion, on motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, and
        unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to adopt the Final Rules filed into the record on
        October 5, 2026, with amendments.

        Vice Chairman Coussan’s motion was to adopt the Final Rules with an amendment to
        Section 601 to read as follows:
        Notwithstanding the foregoing:
           (i)     any jurisdictional utility with a rate proceeding pending before or prescribed by the
                   Commission as of the effective date of this Order shall comply with the
                   requirements of this Order upon the effective date of new rates resulting from such
                   proceedings; and,
           (ii)    any jurisdictional utility that is a party to an existing contract for Franchise
                   Payments with a Political Subdivision that is currently billed in compliance with
                   the Commission’s 2007 Order shall comply with the requirements of this Order as
                   and when contract amendments can be negotiated with said Political Subdivisions,
                   but in no event later than the renewal of existing contracts for Franchise Payments
                   which may only be executed in compliance with this Order and as the same may be
                   amended from time to time.

        Present for Questions/Comments:
        Glenn Edwards – General Counsel for SLEMCO
Ex. 7   U-37463 - Southwestern Electric Power Company, ex parte. In re: Application for approval to
        construct the Hallsville natural gas plant and to convert the Welsh Units 1 and 3 to natural gas.
        In re: Discussion and possible vote on Uncontested Stipulated Settlement.
        After discussion, on motion of Commissioner Campbell, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, and
        unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Staff Report and Recommendation
        filed into the record on September 11, 2026, including the updated Rate Schedule 72 filed into
        the record on October 9, 2026.
        Present for Questions/Comments:
        Bobby Gilliam – Outside Counsel for SWEPCO
        Wesley Hunt – Director of Regulatory Services for SWEPCO
Ex. 8   S-37945 - Washington-St. Tammany Electric Cooperative, Inc., ex parte. In re: Request for
        Letter of Non-Opposition to secure a loan for WST's construction work plan, including
        mortgaging assets related thereto.
        In re: Discussion and possible vote on Staff Report and Recommendation.

        On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, and unanimously
        adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Staff Report and Recommendation filed into the
        record on September 11, 2026.
                                           -3-               Minutes of October 22, 2026 B&E
 Ex. 9    U-29203 - Entergy Gulf States, Inc. and Entergy Louisiana, Inc. In re: Joint Application for
         Interim and Permanent Recovery in Rates of Costs Related to Hurricanes Katrina and Rita;
         U-30981 - Entergy Gulf States Louisiana, L.L.C. and Entergy Louisiana, LLC. In re: Joint
         Application for Recovery in Rates of Costs Related to Hurricanes Gustav and Ike;
         U-32764 - Entergy Louisiana, LLC and Entergy Gulf States Louisiana, LLC. In re: Joint
         Application for Recovery in Rates of Costs Related to Hurricane Isaac, Determination of
         Appropriate Storm Reserve Escrow Amounts and Related Relief;
         U-35991 - Entergy Louisiana, LLC, ex parte. In re: Application for Recovery in Rates of Costs
         Related to Hurricanes Laura, Delta, Zeta and Winter Storm Uri and for Related Relief; and,
         U-36350 - Entergy Louisiana, LLC, ex parte. In re: Application for recovery in rates of costs
         related to Hurricane Ida and for related relief.
         In re: Discussion and possible vote to accept and approve the Annual Report of the
         Louisiana Utilities Restoration Corporation to the Louisiana Public Service Commission
         for the fiscal year 2026, including the annual Operating Budget for fiscal year 2027 and
         the interim and annual Compiled Financial Statements for fiscal year 2026.
         After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and
         unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept and approve the Fiscal Year 2026
         Annual Report of the LURC to the Commission, including the Annual Operating Budget for
         the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027 and interim and compiled annual financial statements of
         the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026.

         Present for Questions/Comments:
         Kieran Spencer – Take Back the Power and Louisiana Party for Socialism and Liberation
         Jamie Watts – Outside Counsel for the Louisiana Utilities Restoration Corporation
Ex. 10   U-35523 - Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: Audit of Fuel Adjustment
         Clause Filings for Entergy Louisiana, LLC for the period of January 2016 through December
         2019.
         In re: Discussion and possible vote on Joint Report.
         On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously
         adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Joint Report filed into the record on October 9,
         2026.
Ex. 11   U-37603 - Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: Audit of Purchase Gas
         Adjustment filings for the natural gas division of Entergy Louisiana, LLC for the period of
         January 2023 through June 30, 2025.

         In re: Discussion and possible vote on Joint Report and Draft Order.

         On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, and unanimously

         record on October 5, 2026.




                                              -4-               Minutes of October 22, 2026 B&E
 Ex. 12   U-37812 - Entergy Louisiana, LLC, ex parte. In re: Application for certification of the Babel -
         Webre 500kV transmission project in accordance with General Order dated September 10,

         In re: Discussion and possible vote on Uncontested Stipulated Settlement.

         unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Uncontested Stipulated Settlement
         filed into the record on September 15, 2026.

         Present for Questions/Comments:
         Devorah Levy-Pearlman – Take Back the Power and Louisiana Party for Socialism and
         Liberation
         Larry Hand – Vice President of Regulatory and Public Affairs for Entergy Louisiana, LLC
         Lane Sisung –Consultant to the LPSC
Ex. 13   U-37838 - Claiborne Electric Cooperative, Inc., ex parte. In re: Request for approval of one-
         year renewal of Formula Rate Plan.
         In re: Discussion and possible vote on Uncontested Stipulated Settlement.
         On motion of Commissioner Campbell, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, and unanimously

         the record on September 3, 2026.
Ex. 14   U-37843 - Magnolia Water Utility Operating Company, LLC, ex parte. In re: Request for a
         Letter of Non-Opposition to the transfer of all of the wastewater system assets owned by St.

         DEFERRED
Ex. 15   U-37904 - Parish Water Company, Inc., ex parte. In re: Request for extension and modification
         of Formula Rate Plan.

         In re: Discussion and possible vote on Uncontested Stipulated Settlement.
         On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously
         adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the
         record on September 17, 2026.
Ex. 16   U-37929 - South Louisiana Electric Cooperative Association, ex parte. In re: Formula Rate
         Plan annual earnings monitoring report for test year ending on December 31, 2025.
         In re: Discussion and possible vote on Joint Report and Draft Order.
         After discussion, on motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Commissioner Campbell,
         with Commissioner Francis and Commission Lewis concurring, and Chairman Skrmetta
         temporarily absent, the Commission voted to accept the Joint Report and issue the draft order
         filed into the record on September 30, 2026.

         Present for Questions/Comments:
         Kara Kantrow – Counsel for SLECA




                                              -5-                Minutes of October 22, 2026 B&E
 Ex. 17   U-38093 - 1803 Electric Cooperative, Inc., ex parte. In re: Application for approval of a Winter
         Capacity Purchase Agreement, including cost recovery.
         In re: Discussion and possible vote to retain United Professionals Company for an under
         $50,000 solicitation.
         On motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Commissioner Campbell, and
         unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to retain UPC for $35,000 in fees and $1,000 in
         expenses for a total not to exceed budget of $36,000.
Ex. 18   X-38068 - Dixie Electric Membership Corporation and Southwest Louisiana Electric
         Membership Corporation. In re: Request for Proposals for long-term Power Purchase
         Contracts, Generating Capacity, and/or Generating Resources pursuant to the Commission's
         General Order dated October 14, 2024 (MBM Order).
         In re: Discussion and possible vote to retain an outside consultant.
         On motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Commissioner Francis, and unanimously
         adopted, the Commission voted to retain United Professionals Company for $89,000 in fees
         and $1,500 in expenses for a total not to exceed budget of $90,500.
Ex. 19   1) Reports

         Based on the comments received by Mayor Monceaux, Chairman Skrmetta directed Staff to
         open an investigation of LAWCO regarding its meter-reading, billing, and collection practices
         over the last five years. Staff was also directed to retain an engineer to evaluate the system,
         and to update the Commission at the December 2026 Business and Executive Session and
         every month thereafter as necessary until the matter is resolved.

         There was no opposition to the directive.

         2) Resolutions
         3) Discussions/Public Comments

         Chad Monceaux, Mayor of Crowley, requested an investigation related to the ongoing high
         water bills and alleged improper meter reading from Louisiana Water Company (LAWCO).

         Present for Questions/Comments
         Kara Kantrow – Outside Counsel for LAWCO
         Roger Simmons – CFO for LAWCO
         -Update from SLECA on its plans to provide electric service to its Lake Lines members.
         Ms. Kantrow provided an update on behalf of SLECA indicating the Cooperative is exploring
         all regulatory and legal options associated with providing electric service to its Lake Lines
         members.
         The Commission directed SLECA to provide public notice of its board meetings to its
         members, as well as to the Commission to ensure all members.
         Present for Questions/Comments:
         Kara Kantrow – Counsel for SLECA
         Sara Boudreaux – Self/Intervenor in Docket No. U-37394




                                               -6-               Minutes of October 22, 2026 B&E
                 4) ERSC/OMS/SPP
                - Discussion and possible vote to ratify interventions of Louisiana Public Service
                Commission in RTO-Related or other Federal Energy Regulatory Proceedings.
                On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously
                adopted, the Commission voted to ratify the actions taken in ER26-3552, ER26-3557, ER26-
                3558, ER26-3650, ER26-3677, and ER26-3756.
                - Discussion and possible vote to ratify votes cast by Commissioner Francis acting as the
                Commission's representative on the Board of Directors of the Organization of MISO
                States.
                On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, with Commissioner
                Campbell and Commission Lewis concurring, and Commissioner Francis abstaining, the
                Commission voted to ratify Commissioner Francis’s votes cast on September 10, 11, 18 and
                October 5, 2026 as the Louisiana Public Service Commission representative to the OMS Board
                of Directors.
                5) Directives
 Ex. 20         R-38096 - Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: Possible amendments to
                Commission General Order dated December 20, 2024 and Special Order 46-2005 (Corrected)
                solely to consider increasing the cap on the current fuel surcharge schedules for nonconsensual
                towing companies and motor carriers.
                In re: Discussion and possible vote on Staff's Proposed Recommendation.
                At the request of Chairman Skrmetta.
                After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and
                unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to adopt Staff’s Proposed Recommendation filed
                into the record on October 16, 2026.
 Ex. 21         U-37394 - South Louisiana Electric Cooperative Association, ex parte. In re: Petition for
                approval of abandonment of electric facilities located in Terrebonne and Lafourche Parishes
                pursuant to Commission General Order dated July 9, 2008 (R-30301).
                In re: Discussion and possible vote on SLECA's Motion for Rehearing.
                At the request of Chairman Skrmetta.
                In re: Possible Executive Session to discuss litigation strategy pursuant to La. R.S. 42:17.
                On motion of Commissioner Campbell, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, and unanimously
                adopted, the Commission voted to enter into Executive Session.
                On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, with Commissioner
                Lewis concurring, and Commissioner Campbell and Commissioner Francis absent, the
                Commission voted to exit Executive Session.
                DEFERRED

On motion of Commissioner Lewis, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, with Vice Chairman Coussan and
Commissioner Francis concurring, and Commissioner Campbell absent, the Commission voted to adjourn.

MEETING ADJOURNED

The next Business and Executive Session will be held on Wednesday, November 18, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. in Baton
Rouge, Louisiana.
